content: Before starting fosamprenavir, inform your doctor or pharmacist about all the products you use, including prescription drugs, nonprescription drugs, and herbal products. To achieve the best therapeutic effect, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals. It is crucial to adhere strictly to the prescribed regimen for this medication and any other HIV medications. Do not skip doses, take more or less than prescribed, or stop taking it without your doctor’s explicit instructions, even for a short period. Common side effects of fosamprenavir include diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, and headache. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to combat pre-existing infections, potentially causing symptoms of those infections to reappear. Additionally, an overactive immune response may occur, which can happen at any time, either shortly after starting HIV treatment or months later. Changes in body fat distribution may occur while taking this medication, such as increased fat in the upper back and abdominal areas and decreased fat in the arms and legs. The cause and long-term effects of these changes are not yet fully understood. Fosamprenavir may also cause a rash, which is usually not serious. However, it can be difficult to distinguish between a common rash and a rare rash that may indicate a severe reaction. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. Before taking fosamprenavir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, amprenavir, or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients, such as propylene glycol in the suspension, which can cause allergic reactions or other issues. Fosamprenavir may increase blood levels of cholesterol and triglycerides, which can also be elevated due to HIV infection itself. This may raise your risk of heart problems, such as a heart attack. Discuss the risks and benefits of treatment with your doctor, as well as strategies to reduce your risk of heart disease. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. HIV treatment can reduce the risk of transmitting the infection to your baby, and fosamprenavir may be part of that treatment. It is unknown whether this medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Certain medications can affect the removal of fosamprenavir from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Examples include apalutamide, etravirine, and rifampin. Fosamprenavir can also influence the removal of other medications from your body, affecting their efficacy. This medication may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods, such as pills, patches, or rings, potentially leading to pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor or pharmacist whether you should use reliable backup birth control methods while taking this medication. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While taking this medication, regular lab and medical tests, such as viral load, T-cell counts, liver function, cholesterol/triglyceride levels, and blood sugar levels, should be conducted. Ensure you attend all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is more than four hours after the missed dose, skip it and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store the tablets at room temperature, away from light and moisture. The suspension can be stored at room temperature or in the refrigerator, as refrigeration may improve its taste. Do not freeze the suspension. Avoid storing this medication in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
